I hear that you feel strongly about this, but I disagree that there's an "objectively better" way to have a conversation. What feels boring and unproductive to you feels meaningful and satisfying to me, just like your preferred style probably feels energizing and engaging for you.

I'm not going to change my preference just because you disagree with it—my likes and dislikes are part of who I am, just like yours are part of you. That said, I can see the value in both approaches: topic-hopping is great for casual, playful chats where you just want to bounce ideas around, and focused conversations are better when you want to really dig into something that matters to you.

Maybe we could try mixing it up sometimes? Start with a focused topic, and if we naturally veer off into other things, go with that flow. That way, we both get to enjoy the parts of conversation that we like.
